subject: Prompt derivatives: ownership, TTL options, and access model (post-demo follow-up)
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Subject: Prompt derivatives: ownership, TTL options, and access model (post-demo follow-up)

Hi Daniel / Lena —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and the things we promised to clarify around prompt/derivative handling so your security & compliance team can validate: 

What Redwood stores by default (hosted API):
- Request metadata (timestamp, model, route) for observability and billing — retained short-term.
- Prompt text + model response ("derivatives") are NOT persisted to long-term storage unless the customer explicitly opts in for analytics or troubleshooting snapshot.
- Ephemeral KV cache used during inference is not written to logs or object storage; it exists in-process and is cleared on session end.

Retention / TTL options we support (configurable per-account or per-route):
- Ephemeral mode (no persistence): 0 days — no derivatives retained.
- Minimal logging: 7 days (default for trial accounts).
- Production retention tiers: 30 / 90 / 365 days — pricing & SLA vary by tier.

Regioning / residency:
- Hosted US region (default), EU region available for customers requesting EU-only storage.
- Dedicated & Private deployments support customer-managed VPC and KMS so data never leaves your network if required.

Embeddings / indexes:
- Embeddings are NOT stored or indexed by default. If you choose "indexing/semantic search" feature, embeddings are written to your dedicated index and retention follows the index TTL.

Access controls & logging:
- All access to stored derivatives is logged (audit trail) and can be routed to your SIEM via syslog/forwarder.
- Role-based access for stored data via Redwood Console; HSM/KMS integrations support customer-managed keys on Private deployments.

Next steps I promised today:
1) Share concise written answers + SOC2 snapshot and a one-page prompt-dataflow diagram (attached).
2) Schedule a security deep-dive with our infra/security lead to go line-by-line on TTL and redaction options.
3) Draft a simple mutual action plan that maps retention tier selection to procurement timing.

Attachments: redwood-prompt-data-primer.pdf (pdf)

If anything above looks off relative to what you heard on the call, flag it and I will correct. Otherwise please confirm which retention tier and region you want us to scope in the MAP.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen

Thanks Stephanie — this aligns with the demo. A few clarifications from our security team after a quick read-through: 

- Confirm whether any prompt text is included in backups / disaster recovery snapshots for Hosted mode. We need an explicit statement that backups can be scoped to exclude derivatives.
- Embeddings: we need the default behavior in writing — you state not stored by default, but can you confirm that when we do opt-in for "indexing", embeddings are stored only in the region we select and retention follows the index TTL (no cross-region replication)?
- Redaction: for PII we want an automated pre-ingest redaction option (name/ssn/email) and a separate manual redaction API for post-hoc removals. Is that already available or on the roadmap?

Also, our legal team will want a retention commitment in writing (we're currently evaluating 30 vs 90 days) and a pointer to the exact SOC2 scope in the snapshot you mentioned.

Can we schedule the security deep-dive next week (preferably Tue/Wed morning UTC)?

Thanks,
Daniel Morris
CTO, Brightway Health

Subject: Re: Prompt derivatives: ownership, TTL options, and access model (post-demo follow-up)

Hi Daniel / Lena — thanks for the quick follow-up and useful questions. Answers inline below.

- Backups / DR snapshots:
  * Hosted mode: derivatives are excluded from long-term object-storage backups by default. We keep short-lived operational logs for a maximum of 7 days (unless you request otherwise). Backups can be scoped to exclude derivative payloads — we will add this exclusion clause to the MSA addendum.

- Embeddings & indexing: 
  * Confirmed: embeddings are not persisted unless you enable the "indexing" feature. When enabled, embeddings are stored in the region you select and do not replicate cross-region unless you explicitly enable multi-region. Index TTLs are configurable per-index (30/90/365).

- Redaction options: 
  * Pre-ingest PII redaction: available as a configuration hook (regex + ML classifiers) — we can enable that before any prompt is persisted for analytics.
  * Post-hoc removal API: available for Dedicated & Private today; for Hosted we provide a removal workflow that runs within 24-72 hours and is auditable. We will include the SLA for removals in the MAP.

- Retention commitments:
  * For the MAP, we can commit to the 30-day production tier (standard) with an option to move to 90 days under a 12-month commit. For higher guarantees (e.g., EU-only residency and strict DR exclusions) we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment.

Attachments (as promised):
- SOC2_snapshot_2026.pdf (redacted scope summary)
- prompt-dataflow-diagram.png (one-page flow showing where derivatives live and what we persist)
- redwood-prompt-data-primer.pdf (brief primer on TTLs and redaction toggles)

Next steps:
1) Daniel / Lena — please confirm preferred retention tier (30 / 90 / ephemeral) and target region.
2) I'll book the security deep-dive for Tue Dec 8 09:30–10:30 UTC unless you prefer another slot.
3) Ben / Marissa — I'll share the MAP draft link and update it with the retention selection once Brightway confirms.

If this all looks good I will escalate to Legal for the MSA addendum draft.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
